topic: Dog years: the 1-to-7 rule is off; one study of 104 Labradors puts a 1-year-old dog at about 31 human years
searched_phrase: how old is my dog in human years (YouTube and Google rank 1, seed 'how old is my dog in human')
fact: Wang et al., Cell Systems 2020, 104 Labrador retrievers: human_age = 16 ln(dog_age) + 31 (full text, PMC7484147). So a 1-year-old Lab is about 31, a 2-year-old about 42.
second_fact: Abstract: comparing dog and human methylomes 'reveals a nonlinear relationship that translates dog-to-human years' and lines up milestones like puberty.
do_not_say: Do not say it works for every breed (Labradors only), do not say it is the final formula; keep 'in one study'.
evidence: Suggestion re-pulled 11/12 (holds). Researcher: 1 Short of 15 (an app advert, 730 views); winners are SciShow, Bright Side, Insider. Not re-searched. No small-channel outlier.

topic: Do cats always land on their feet? In two vet studies most cats that fell from buildings survived, but many broke bones
searched_phrase: do cats always land on their feet (YouTube rank 6, seed 'do cats')
fact: Vnuk et al. 2004, 119 cats brought to a Zagreb vet clinic after falls (average 4 stories): 96.5% survived; 46.2% had broken limbs. Falls from the 7th story up were linked to worse injuries.
second_fact: Whitney and Mehlhaff 1987, 132 cats in New York: 90% had chest injuries; 'Ninety percent of the treated cats survived' (treated = 67% of the cats).
do_not_say: Do not say cats always land on their feet or that falls are safe; survival is only for cats that reached a vet (deaths at the scene not counted). Do not say higher falls are safer.
evidence: Suggestion re-pulled 11/12 (holds, rank 6). ytsearch15 re-run 11/12: 2 Shorts of 15; donjgm 'Cats don't always land on their feet' 22,335 views (29 s), channel median not measurable (Shorts tab pull failed); OurNest 7 views.
